content: 1. Famotidine, when administered at a dose of 5 mg/kg twice daily for 6-12 weeks, should not exceed 40 mg twice daily. For children under 12 years of age, the safety and efficacy of famotidine have not been established. For individuals over 12 years, a dose of 10-20 mg every 12 hours is recommended. Famotidine may be taken 15-60 minutes before consuming foods that could trigger heartburn. 2. Famotidine decreases the plasma concentration and efficacy of atazanavir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or consider using an alternative drug. Atazanavir's solubility decreases as pH increases, leading to significantly reduced plasma levels when coadministered with H2-receptor antagonists (H2RAs). For treatment-naïve patients, atazanavir should be taken simultaneously with the H2RA or at least 10 hours afterward. For treatment-experienced patients, refer to dosage adjustment recommendations. 3. Famotidine reduces the plasma concentration and efficacy of bosutinib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or consider using an alternative drug. 4. Famotidine decreases the plasma concentration and efficacy of dapsone by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or consider using an alternative drug. 5. Famotidine reduces the plasma concentration and efficacy of dasatinib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or consider using an alternative drug. 6. Famotidine increases the plasma concentration and effect of digoxin by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or consider using an alternative drug. 7. Famotidine decreases the plasma concentration and efficacy of indinavir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or consider using an alternative drug. 8. Famotidine reduces the plasma concentration and efficacy of infigratinib (DSC) by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or consider using an alternative drug. If coadministration with an acid-reducing agent cannot be avoided, administer infigratinib 2 hours before or 10 hours after the H2-antagonist. 9. Famotidine decreases the plasma concentration and efficacy of itraconazole by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or consider using an alternative drug. 10. Famotidine reduces the plasma concentration and efficacy of ketoconazole by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or consider using an alternative drug. 11. Famotidine decreases the plasma concentration and efficacy of levoketoconazole by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or consider using an alternative drug. 12. Mefloquine increases the toxicity of famotidine by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or consider using an alternative drug. Mefloquine may enhance the QTc-prolonging effect of high-risk QTc-prolonging agents. 13. Famotidine reduces the plasma concentration and efficacy of neratinib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or consider using an alternative drug. 14. Famotidine decreases the plasma concentration and efficacy of pazopanib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration of pazopanib with drugs that raise gastric pH. Consider using short-acting antacids instead of proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) and H2-antagonists, and separate antacid and pazopanib dosing by several hours. 15. Famotidine increases the plasma concentration and effect of pexidartinib by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or consider using an alternative drug. Administer pexidartinib 2 hours before or 10 hours after taking an H2-antagonist. 16. Famotidine and pimozide increase each other's toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or consider using an alternative drug. 17. Famotidine decreases the plasma concentration and efficacy of ponatinib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or consider using an alternative drug. 18. Famotidine increases the plasma concentration and effect of risedronate by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the delayed-release formulation of risedronate. Famotidine accelerates the pH-sensitive dissolution of delayed-release risedronate, potentially affecting its release properties and absorption in the duodenum. 19. Famotidine and secretin interaction may cause a hyperresponse in gastrin secretion during stimulation testing with secretin, falsely suggesting gastrinoma. Discontinue H2-receptor antagonists at least 2 days before administering secretin to aid in the diagnosis of gastrinoma. 20. Famotidine decreases the plasma concentration and efficacy of sotorasib by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider using an alternative drug. If coadministration with an acid-reducing agent cannot be avoided, administer sotorasib 4 hours before or 10 hours after a locally-acting antacid. 21. Famotidine reduces the plasma concentration and efficacy of sparsentan by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or consider using an alternative drug. H2-antagonists may decrease sparsentan exposure, potentially reducing its efficacy. 22. Tafenoquine increases the plasma concentration and effect of famotidine by inhibiting organic cation transporter-2 (OCT2) and multidrug and toxin extrusion (MATE) transporters in vitro. Avoid coadministration with OCT2 or MATE substrates. If coadministration cannot be avoided, monitor for substrate-related toxicities and consider dosage reduction based on product labeling of the coadministered drug. 23. Famotidine decreases the plasma concentration and efficacy of acalabrutinib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Administer acalabrutinib 2 hours before an H2-receptor antagonist. 24. Famotidine decreases the plasma concentration and efficacy of budesonide by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Coadministration with drugs that increase gastric pH may cause extended-release budesonide tablets to prematurely dissolve, potentially affecting their release properties and absorption in the duodenum. 25. Famotidine decreases the plasma concentration and efficacy of carbonyl iron by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Famotidine decreases the plasma concentration and efficacy of cefdinir, cefditoren, cefpodoxime, and cefuroxime by increasing gastric pH. These interactions apply only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Famotidine decreases the plasma concentration and efficacy of crizotinib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Drugs that elevate gastric pH may decrease the solubility of crizotinib and subsequently reduce its bioavailability. However, no formal studies have been conducted. 28. Famotidine increases the plasma concentration and effect of cyclosporine by an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Delayed resorption of cyclosporine has been reported when coadministered with famotidine. 29. Famotidine decreases the plasma concentration and efficacy of dabrafenib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Drugs that alter upper gastrointestinal tract pH (e.g., PPIs, H2-blockers, antacids) may decrease dabrafenib solubility and reduce its bioavailability. 30. Famotidine increases the plasma concentration and effect of dexmethylphenidate by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy and monitor closely. This applies only to the extended-release formulation. 31. Famotidine increases the plasma concentration and effect of erdafitinib by decreasing renal clearance. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Consider alternatives that are not OCT2 substrates or consider reducing the dose of OCT2 substrates based on tolerability. 32. Famotidine decreases the plasma concentration and efficacy of erlotinib by an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Avoid combination when possible. If concurrent use is required, erlotinib should be taken 10 hours after an H2-antagonist and at least 2 hours before the next dose of the H2-antagonist. 33. Famotidine decreases the plasma concentration and efficacy of ferric maltol, ferrous fumarate, ferrous gluconate, and ferrous sulfate by increasing gastric pH. These interactions apply only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Famotidine decreases the plasma concentration and efficacy of fosamprenavir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Famotidine decreases the plasma concentration and efficacy of gefitinib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Separate gefitinib and H2-antagonist doses by at least 6 hours. 36. Famotidine increases the plasma concentration and effect of glipizide and glyburide by increasing gastric pH. These interactions apply only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Famotidine decreases the plasma concentration and efficacy of iron dextran complex, iron sucrose, and polysaccharide iron by increasing gastric pH. These interactions apply only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Famotidine decreases the plasma concentration and efficacy of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir by an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Ledipasvir solubility decreases as pH increases; drugs that increase gastric pH are expected to decrease levels of ledipasvir. H2-receptor antagonists may be administered simultaneously with or 12 hours apart from ledipasvir/sofosbuvir at a dose that does not exceed doses comparable to famotidine 40 mg BID. 39. Famotidine decreases the plasma concentration and efficacy of mesalamine by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 40. Famotidine increases the plasma concentration and effect of methylphenidate by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy and monitor closely. This applies only to the extended-release formulation. 41. Famotidine and mifepristone increase each other's toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Famotidine decreases the plasma concentration and efficacy of mycophenolate by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Famotidine decreases the plasma concentration and efficacy of nelfinavir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Famotidine decreases the plasma concentration and efficacy of nilotinib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Avoid this interaction by administering H2-antagonists 10 hours after or 2 hours before nilotinib. 45. Famotidine decreases the plasma concentration and efficacy of posaconazole by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Pretomanid increases the plasma concentration and effect of famotidine by inhibiting OAT3. Modify therapy and monitor closely. In vitro studies demonstrated that pretomanid significantly inhibits OAT3; monitor for increased adverse effects and consider dosage reduction for OAT3 substrates. 47. Famotidine decreases the plasma concentration and efficacy of rilpivirine by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Concurrent use may cause treatment failure and/or the development of rilpivirine or NNRTI resistance due to decreased levels. Administer H2-antagonists at least 12 hours before or at least 4 hours after rilpivirine. 48. Famotidine decreases the plasma concentration and efficacy of rose hips by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Famotidine increases the plasma concentration and effect of serdexmethylphenidate/dexmethylphenidate by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy and monitor closely. This applies only to the extended-release formulation. 50. Famotidine decreases the plasma concentration and efficacy of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Velpatasvir solubility decreases as gastric pH increases (practically insoluble at pH >5). H2-receptor antagonists may be administered simultaneously with or 12 hours apart from sofosbuvir/velpatasvir at a dose that does not exceed doses comparable to famotidine 40 mg BID. 51. Vadadustat increases the plasma concentration and effect of famotidine by an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Vadadustat may increase exposure of OAT3 substrates. Monitor for signs of adverse effects of OAT3 substrates and reduce substrate dose in accordance with their product labeling. 52. Famotidine increases the plasma concentration and effect of varenicline by decreasing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. 53. Famotidine decreases the plasma concentration and efficacy of vismodegib by an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Drugs that increase gastric pH alter vismodegib solubility and therefore reduce bioavailability; the effect on efficacy is unknown. 54. Famotidine increases the plasma concentration and effect of alendronate by an unspecified interaction mechanism. Monitor for an increase in alendronate side effects. 55. Famotidine decreases the plasma concentration and efficacy of aripiprazole by an unspecified interaction mechanism. Monitor closely.
